subject: Streaming + third-party synthesizer: truncation observed in prefetch flows
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
To: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, logan_wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Streaming + third-party synthesizer: truncation observed in prefetch flows

Claire at Synthetic Health hit a blocking issue in their demo integration: when they enable our SDK prefetch with their third-party speech synthesizer in the response path, generated passages occasionally truncate mid-sentence and the client receives a truncated audio payload. I captured the customer's sample request and the streaming logs (attached).

Summary:
- Customer flow: Redwood hosted runtime -> streaming tokens -> their TTS adapter consumes chunks and reassembles audio.
- Symptom: intermittent truncation roughly ~1/50 requests, typically on long outputs or when the first token of the final chunk is a punctuation char.
- Repro: Claire attached a small sample request (synth-request-sample.json) and a stream log snippet that shows an abrupt stop with no error returned from Redwood (stream finishes).

Impact: P1 for the customer demo next Wednesday (they want to present live). They're on a trial and this would significantly reduce confidence.

Ask (short):
1) Can runtime accept a short-term opt-in flag from the SDK to force boundary-safe chunking (e.g. break tokens on full-word boundaries or insert a synthetic sentinel at chunk boundaries) so the customer's TTS doesn't drop audio?
2) Can we add a telemetry event (stream_boundary_mismatch) so we can quickly detect if the fix helps?

If runtime can't safely roll this, we'll need a compensating mitigation (dedicated short-term capacity + client-side prefetch disable or an SDK shim). Please reply with feasibility and a rough implementation ETA. I can escalate a small credit if necessary.

Attachments: synth-request-sample.json, stream-log-snippet.txt

Thanks,
Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Streaming + third-party synthesizer: truncation observed in prefetch flows

Quick read-through of the log: looks like the client receives a final chunk that is byte-truncated relative to the last token boundary. Two likely root causes:
- Our streaming chunking aligns to internal token frames (optimised for throughput) which may split UTF-8 sequences or punctuation that some TTS adapters treat as sentence terminators.
- A race in prefetch flushing where the SDK signals 'end-of-stream' before the final token buffer is fully serialized to the network socket.

Temporary mitigations I can see from the SDK side (low-friction):
- Expose an SDK flag: X-Redwood-Stream-Mode: safe-word-boundary (causes client SDK to buffer last N bytes and ensure full-token boundary).
- Or: allow customers to opt out of prefetch for streaming requests (instantly available but higher latency).

If runtime wants an alternate: add a lightweight suffix sentinel token on our end (runtime appends a NOOP token that TTS will ignore) — but that touches model output and could affect token counts/costs.

Telemetry: agree on stream_boundary_mismatch with fields: request_id, model, route, boundary_type. Happy to help instrument on SDK side once the event spec is defined.

My preference: short-term SDK flag + telemetry; medium-term runtime fix depending on perf risk.

- Logan
Logan Wright
Sales Engineering
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Streaming + third-party synthesizer: truncation observed in prefetch flows

Thanks for the summary. Short answers:
- We can implement a runtime-level opt-in that causes the serving runtime to align emit points to codepoint/token boundaries, but this will add a measurable CPU/latency cost in the hot path (especially on quantized kernels).
- Suffix sentinel insertion is safer but will change output length; we'd need to clearly signal that in the API contract and offer an opt-out.

Before we change production code we need a minimal reproducible test (native harness) to run across our staging fleet. If you can get a small repro that reproduces ~1/50 requests, we can run it and measure perf overhead. If the repro is small, we can do a canary rollout to 1% of traffic for the affected route.

I can own a quick PoC for the runtime opt-in flag, but we'll need dev_patel to help wire the SDK header -> runtime config path and add the new telemetry event. ETA: PoC in 3 business days, canary in 7 assuming repro exists. If it's blocked, we'll push SDK-side buffering as an interim.

-Jonas
Jonas Weber
Runtime Engineering Lead
